summary: Backend smoke test complete. Auth, clients, contracts, manual events, ICS export, invoice PDF, dashboard stats all work. CRITICAL bug: POST /api/planning/generate and POST /api/planning/reschedule return 500 because response payload includes freshly-inserted Mongo docs that carry '_id' (ObjectId) after insert_many, which FastAPI cannot serialize. DB inserts still succeed and status transitions work — but any client using these endpoints will see errors.
passed: GET /api/auth/me without token -> 401; with seeded Bearer token -> 200 (correct user)

POST/GET/PUT /api/clients (with address 'Piazza Duomo 1, Milano') -> 200. Nominatim returned 403 (geocoding provider rate-limited from server IP), but endpoints still respond 200 with lat/lng null as allowed.

POST /api/contracts (total_days=5, priority='high', daily_rate=500) -> 200; PUT full-body -> 200; DELETE not exercised but /complete -> 200; status transitions active->planned->invoiced verified via list
Planning algorithm works internally: 5 weekday interventions created (skips Sat/Sun), status flips to 'planned' in DB
Manual events blocking: manual event on 2026-09-15 correctly excluded during regenerate; planner shifted to next weekday 2026-09-18
GET /api/calendar/export.ics?user_id&token -> 200, content-type text/calendar, 5 VEVENTs including intervention data (SUMMARY, LOCATION, DESCRIPTION)
POST /api/invoices/generate regime_forfettario=true -> 200 application/pdf (%PDF- header, 2335 bytes); with VAT 22 & withholding 20 -> 200 application/pdf; contract status becomes 'invoiced'
GET /api/dashboard/stats returns active_contracts, total_contracts, clients_count, interventions_planned, total_workdays, projected_revenue, upcoming[]

failed.issue: Returns HTTP 500 (Internal Server Error) even though interventions are inserted correctly and contract status is updated. Root cause: after `db.interventions.insert_many(new_interventions)` (server.py L445), Motor mutates the list in-place appending Mongo `_id` (ObjectId) to each dict; those dicts are then returned in the response body (L449 `return {..., 'interventions': new_interventions}`) and FastAPI's jsonable_encoder throws: `TypeError: 'ObjectId' object is not iterable`.
failed.evidence: backend.err.log traceback: fastapi/encoders.py:322 -> `TypeError: 'ObjectId' object is not iterable`. Reproduced twice. HTTP response body: 'Internal Server Error'.

failed.issue: Returns HTTP 500 for the same reason — it delegates to generate_planning() and inherits the ObjectId serialization bug (server.py L519).
failed.evidence: curl -X POST /api/planning/reschedule -> HTTP:500 'Internal Server Error'; interventions actually get recreated in DB correctly (verified with GET /api/interventions).

failed.issue: Requires the full ContractIn payload (client_id, title, total_days...); partial-body updates return 422. Not necessarily a bug, but the review request implied partial update. Consumer must send the entire ContractIn.
failed.evidence: PUT with {"notes":"upd"} -> 422 missing client_id/title/total_days. Full-body PUT -> 200.

failed.issue: Returned URL uses `http://` and an internal/alternate host (job-scheduler-pro-12.cluster-7.preview.emergentcf.cloud) which 301-redirects to HTML when fetched. Directly calling /api/calendar/export.ics on the real REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL works fine over HTTPS. The subscribe-url should return the public HTTPS URL that Google Calendar can subscribe to.
failed.evidence: curl subscribe-url -> {"url":"http://job-scheduler-pro-12.cluster-7.preview.emergentcf.cloud/api/calendar/export.ics?..."}; GET that URL -> 301 text/html. Direct HTTPS on REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL -> 200 text/calendar with 5 VEVENTs.

failed.issue: Nominatim returns 403 Forbidden from the backend host — likely missing User-Agent or blocked IP. lat/lng always null. Endpoint still returns 200 so it does not block clients, but the travel-optimization feature will fall back to arbitrary ordering.

action_items: Fix planning/generate & planning/reschedule 500: either exclude `_id` from `new_interventions` before returning (e.g. build response dicts with the Pydantic Intervention model, or `for iv in new_interventions: iv.pop('_id', None)` after insert_many), or return a projection-based fetch. This unblocks all frontend planning flows.
Fix /api/calendar/subscribe-url to build the URL from the request's public HTTPS origin (REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL) or force https:// scheme, so Google Calendar can subscribe.
Add a valid User-Agent header (Nominatim TOS requires it, e.g. 'PlanOp/1.0 (contact-email)') in the geocode() httpx call to fix the 403.
Consider making ContractIn fields Optional for PUT or provide a separate ContractUpdate schema.
